gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.
'Firstly' opens a sequence of instructions; eventually/finally close one.

gaps.sentence: The plan was expensive; ___, the board approved it.
gaps.explanation: The approval happens in spite of the cost: nevertheless signals concession.

gaps.sentence: ___ he apologises, I'm not speaking to him again.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' = if he does not apologise; the main clause states the default outcome.

gaps.sentence: ___ heavy demand, tickets are limited to four per person.
gaps.explanation: 'Owing to + noun' introduces the cause in announcements and notices.

gaps.sentence: He is far from lazy; ___, he trains six hours a day.
gaps.explanation: 'On the contrary' rejects the description and states the reverse, more strongly.

gaps.sentence: She earns a very good salary; ___, she never seems to have any money.
gaps.explanation: 'Yet' contrasts two facts, like but, in a slightly more formal way.

gaps.sentence: ___ his impressive qualifications, he wasn't even shortlisted.
